global_read: global.json (17:37) shows a calm tape tilted slightly defensive rather than risk-on. S&P -0.17% 1d / Dow -0.20% 1d -- a mild pullback, though both remain up over the month (+2.8%/+2.0%). VIX ticked up +4.84% 1d to 14.94 but is still deep in low-fear territory (-20.4% 1mo) -- a small wobble, not a stress signal. Gold's safe-haven bid is the standout: +1.45% 1d and +10.75% 1mo -- a persistent hedge flow that argues for some caution even as headline indices sit near highs. Brent is +0.62% 1d / +1.1% 1mo -- a mild, not acute, import-bill/PKR headwind. USD/PKR is essentially flat (+0.4% 1d, -0.07% 1mo) while DXY is soft (-0.19% 1d, -1.26% 1mo) -- the rupee is holding on its own. Net: a neutral global backdrop for PSX today -- no fresh shock, but gold's strength and the VIX uptick are a mild caution flag against leaning risk-on.
drivers: SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% on 2026-07-27 (second consecutive FY27 hold); next MPC confirmed 2026-09-14, reverified this run with no interim decision since (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40425595)

PBS headline CPI for July 2026 confirmed at 9.2% YoY (down from June's 11.1%, flattered by a low July-2025 base); August print not yet released as of this run (https://tradingeconomics.com/pakistan/inflation-cpi)

SBP-held FX reserves rose to $17.057bn for the week ended 2026-08-07 (+$14mn), a third straight modest weekly gain; total liquid reserves (SBP+banks) $22.498bn, import cover ~2.5 months -- fresh print this run, updated from the prior $17.04bn (week ended 2026-07-31) (https://www.momentumpakistan.com/blog/pakistan-sbp-reserves-rise-by-just-14-million-as-import-cover-holds-at-25-months-2026-08-13-20-34-40-tkxxjsrncb-34831)

2026-08-05 T-bill auction remains the latest settled: 6M cutoff 11.70% (Rs111.05bn accepted vs Rs358.65bn bid), 12M cutoff 11.9490%, Rs939.11bn raised overall; next MTB auction confirmed for 2026-08-19 (Rs200bn target), correcting the prior run's expected 2026-08-14 date (https://mettisglobal.news/sbp-to-conduct-another-t-bills-buyback-auction-with-rs200bn-target/)

July 2026 workers' remittances hit $3.63bn, up 13% YoY and 4.5% MoM -- confirms the strong-inflow trend carrying into FY27, no fresher monthly print yet (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40434250/jul-remittances-soar-13pc-to-usd36bn-yoy)

FY26 current account closed at a $139mn deficit (0.03% of GDP) despite record remittances, as high imports offset inflows; no July 2026 (FY27) monthly current-account print located yet as of this run (https://www.dawn.com/news/2016383)
